components.description: Backend service implementing OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow and refresh tokens, JWT-based session handling, strict per-tenant token isolation, and per-tenant rate limiting. Implemented using Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL for persistent storage and Redis for caches/queues/rate-limiting primitives. Includes tests, basic deployment configuration and security hardening appropriate for a regulated fintech.

assumptions: Estimate derived from a single closely matching historical component (BUD-2024-001). The calculation used the historical 120h median plus a 15% contingency -> 138h.

Scope included: implementation of OAuth2 authorization code + refresh tokens, JWT session management, per-tenant token isolation, per-tenant rate limiting, unit/integration tests, security hardening (secure storage of keys, token revocation flows, audit logging), and basic deployment automation (CI/CD pipelines, containerization).

Assumes existing Rails/Postgres/Redis infrastructure and an experienced in-house Rails team to integrate the new service. Assumes standard non-exotic regulatory requirements (audit logs, traceability) but not full certification or external audit coordination.

Not included: client-side work (front-end or mobile SDKs), long-term maintenance/operational support beyond initial handover, integration with third-party identity providers beyond standard OAuth flows unless explicitly requested, major organizational compliance activities or legal reviews.

Confidence note: only one directly relevant historical reference was found (BUD-2024-001). While it is a close match (finance sector, same feature set), the reference pool is small — unknowns (detailed SSO/provider integrations, extremely strict regulator-required processes, or complex tenancy models) could increase effort. Recommend a short follow-up scoping session to firm up integrations and regulatory detail before fixed-price contracting.
